summary: Fawad Khan works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Master's in Archaeology from the University of Peshawar and a PhD from Quaid-i-Azam University. In 2022, he was Assistant Curator at the Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Fazun (1902–1980) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Wuchang Buddhist Institute, Beijing Institute of Tibetan Studies, and Drepung Monastery under numerous teachers, including Taixu. He founded the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and later served as director of the Buddhist Academy of China.

Federico Squarcini (b. 1967) works in Indology and philosophy. He held posts at Ca' Foscari University of Venice around 2011, served as Series Editor for Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies (~2010), and joined the editorial board of Marco Polo around 2020.

Feng Youlan (1895–1990) was a philosopher and sinologist. He studied at Central China Normal University, Peking University, Tsinghua University, and Columbia University. He taught at Tsinghua University (~1928–1952) and was a visiting professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1946–1947).
Ferdinand Benary (1805–1880) studied under Franz Bopp between ~1827 and 1829. In 1831, he became an extraordinary professor in the theological faculty at the University of Berlin.

Ferdinand Christian Baur (1792–1860) worked in religious studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Tübinger Stift and the University of Tübingen (~1809–1814), where he subsequently held an academic post from circa 1826 until 1860.

Ferdinand Diederich Lessing (1882–1961) was a scholar of sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as a teacher at both the University of Berlin and the University of California, Berkeley.

Ferdinand Hitzig (1807–1875) specialized in religious studies and linguistics. He studied under Heinrich Ewald (~1828–1829) and held posts at the University of Zurich (~1833–1861) and the University of Heidelberg (~1861–1875).

Ferdinand Justi (1837–1907) was a linguist and Iranian/Central Asian specialist. He studied under Theodor Benfey at Göttingen and habilitated at Marburg, where he became professor of comparative linguistics and Germanic philology and served as Rektor (1887–1888).

Ferdinand Lessing (1882–1961) was a sinologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Berlin and held positions at Peking University, the University of Berlin, the Ethnological Museum of Berlin, and the University of California, Berkeley.

Ferdinand Sommer (1875–1962) was a linguist and Indologist. He earned his doctorate under Rudolf Thurneysen at Freiburg and completed his Habilitation at Leipzig. He held professorships at Basel, Rostock, Jena, Bonn, and Munich (~1926–1951).

Ferdinand de Saussure (1857–1913) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and EPHE under scholars including Curtius and Brugmann. He held teaching posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, University of Paris, and University of Geneva.

Ferdinand von Eckstein (1790–1861) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Friedrich Creuzer (~1807–1809), founded Le Catholique in 1826, and was a member of the Société Asiatique from circa 1826 to 1861.
Ferenc Ruzsa (b. 1957) is an Indologist and philosopher. He attended Fazekas Mihály Gimnázium (~1971–1975) and completed his studies at Eötvös Loránd University (~1976–1982).

Fernand Meyer is a scholar in the field of Tibetology. He held academic posts at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (CNRS) and at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested in 2004).
Fernando Jose Benetti works in the field of Buddhist studies. He studied at Nalanda University, where he was supervised for his doctorate by Aleksandra Wenta (attested 2018).

Fernando Tola (1915–2017) studied at the National University of San Marcos. Active in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, he held posts at the University of Buenos Aires (~1969–1985) and served as director of the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (~1989–2017).
The Fifth Karma Kuchen (b. 1970) is a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Penor Rinpoche as his heart son and succeeded him in 2000.

Filippo De Filippi (1869–1938) was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the University of Bologna (~1899–1903) and the University of Genoa.

Filippo Marsili is a scholar in sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley under Patricia Berger, Corrado Pensa, and Arcangela Santoro, and later held a post at Saint Louis University.
